units.title: Taxonomy
units.intro:
Classification groups living things so we can name, compare and study them. **Binomial:** Genus species (Homo sapiens) — italic or underlined. Keys: paired choices (dichotomous) to identify a specimen.

**Five kingdoms** in this book: Monera (bacteria, prokaryote), Protista (mostly unicellular eukaryotes), Fungi (heterotroph, chitin wall, spores), Plantae (multicellular, cellulose, photosynthesise), Animalia (multicellular, ingest food, no wall).

cards.title: 2.1 The Importance of Classification
body: From early times humans have found it convenient to classify plants and animals according to their usage, habit or size.
For example plants can be classified according to their use as edible, poisonous or medicinal plants.
According to their characteristics plants can be divided into herbs, shrubs, and trees.
The branch of biology that deals with the naming and classification of organisms is called taxonomy.
A biologist who specializes in this field of study is called a taxonomist.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Under the five-kingdom classification system, which of the following kingdoms consists entirely of prokaryotic unicellular organisms?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Check the cellular status of each kingdom**
*   Kingdom Protista consists of eukaryotic organisms (mostly unicellular).
*   Kingdom Fungi consists of eukaryotic, multicellular, or unicellular (yeast) saprophytes.
*   Kingdom Plantae consists of eukaryotic multicellular autotrophs.
*   Kingdom Monera consists of all prokaryotic unicellular organisms (bacteria and cyanobacteria).

**Final Result:**
**Kingdom Monera** is the correct answer.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following organisms moves using temporary extensions of the cytoplasm called pseudopodia ('false feet')?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify locomotion organs of protists**
* *Paramecium* moves using regular rows of short hair-like **cilia**.
* *Trypanosoma* and *Euglena* move using whip-like **flagella**.
* *Amoeba* moves by flowing cytoplasm into temporary projections called **pseudopodia**.

**Final Result:**
**Amoeba** is the correct answer.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following is the correct sequence of classification in ascending order?
cards.why:
**Logic:**
**Ascending order** means from the most specific (smallest group) to the most general (largest group).
The hierarchy is: **Species $$\rightarrow$$ Genus $$\rightarrow$$ Family $$\rightarrow$$ Order $$\rightarrow$$ Class $$\rightarrow$$ Phylum $$\rightarrow$$ Kingdom**.
(Note: 'genes' in the options refers to 'Genus').

**Result:**
Choice C follows the correct order.

cards.title: The Five-Kingdom Classification
body: Plants: mosses (no true tubes) → ferns (spores, vascular) → gymnosperms (naked seed) → angiosperms (flower, fruit). Animals: at least know invertebrate vs vertebrate, and fish / amphibian / reptile / bird / mammal traits (scales, wet skin, eggs on land, feathers, hair + milk).

cards.title: 2.3.1 Kingdom Monera
body: All members of the kingdom monera are prokaryotic and unicellular.
The kingdom includes organisms like bacteria and cyanobacteria (formerly known as blue-green algae).
Bacteria are simple and most abundant microorganisms.
Mode of Nutrition The means whereby an organism assimilates its food is called nutrition.

cards.title: 2.3.2 Kingdom Protista
body: Kingdom protista includes many simple eukaryotes.
All are aerobic and have mitochondria for cellular respiration.
Most of them reproduce or grow by binary fission and conjugation.
Many can form cysts (an outer covering) in adverse conditions.

cards.title: 2.3.3 Kingdom Fungi
body: Fungi are filamentous eukaryotes with a saprophytic mode of nutrition.
Fungal filaments are known as hyphae and a mass of hyphae is called a mycelium (plural: mycelia).
Fungi are very important in the environment as decomposers.
Fungi reproduce both asexually and sexually by spore formation.

cards.title: 2.3.4 Kingdom Plantae
body: Members of the kingdom plantae are multicellular eukaryotes that have cell walls made of cellulose.
Plants store their food in the form of starch.
The life cycle of plants is a complex alternation of generations.
In the life cycle, the sporophyte generation alternates with the gametophyte generation.

cards.title: 2.3.5 Kingdom Animalia
body: All animals are composed of eukaryotic cells.
A fundamental aspect of the organization of an animal body is the body shape, form, and manner in which the body parts are arranged.
A structure that allows an animal to be divided into parts of an equal shape and size, and a similar position to the line of division is called symmetry.
Symmetry is used to describe the arrangement of body structures with reference to the body axis.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following is a physical adaptation of birds specifically suited to reduce body weight for efficient flight?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify bird adaptations for flight**
* Feathers provide insulation and aid in flying, but hollow bones specifically reduce overall skeletal density and weight to allow the bird to stay airborne easily.
* A four-chambered heart maintains efficient oxygen transport but does not affect body weight directly.

**Final Result:**
**Presence of hollow bones**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: What highly contagious viral disease of hoofed animals (like cattle and pigs) causes painful blisters on the mouth and feet, leading to lameness?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify animal diseases**
* Anthrax is caused by a bacterium (*Bacillus anthracis*).
* Salmonellosis is caused by *Salmonella* bacteria.
* Rabies is a viral disease affecting mammalian central nervous systems.
* Foot-and-mouth disease is a highly contagious viral disease of hoofed animals causing blisters on the mouth and feet.

**Final Result:**
**Foot-and-mouth disease**.

The gametophyte plant is an independent, tiny heart-shaped structure called a prothallus.
The tiny animals in plankton are known as zooplankton.
The spore-bearing plant is known as the sporophyte.

tips.text: In biology, organisms are classified into groups according to their similarities and differences in structure.
The system of classification that we use today in biology was first developed by Carl Linnaeus, the “father” of modern taxonomy.

He classified organisms into a hierarchy of taxonomic ranks that include the kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus and species. He also introduced the system of naming organisms, the binomial nomenclature.
How does one identify plants found in the school compound as herbs, shrubs or trees? 2.
How are animals around your school compound identified as vertebrates or invertebrates?

Most books that enable us to find out about the names of organisms make use of what is called a “key”. Such a key consists of a series of questions, which, when answered, lead one to name the specimen.
In identifying organisms different types of keys are used by taxonomists, of which the dichotomous key is familiar in botanical and zoological works.
The dichotomous key consists of a series of mutually exclusive couplets (pairs of statements).
At each couplet a decision has to be taken to follow one lead or the other. Each statement of a pair will lead the reader to a taxon or to a further couplet.

At each step the number of possible taxa with which the unknown specimen can be identified is successively reduced until there is only one possibility. It is possible to construct a dichotomous key in the following way: a.

questions.answer: To organise, name, and show relatedness.
why: Classification sorts the huge variety of organisms into groups, gives each a universal name, makes them easier to study and shows how they are related.

similar.q: The name 'Red Sea' is very much associated with  A) Trypanosoma.  B) Cyanobacteria.  C) Mushroom.  D) Sarcodina.  E) Plasmodium.
similar.a: B. Cyanobacteria. — The Red Sea is named after blooms of a cyanobacterium (Trichodesmium) with red pigment that periodically colour the water. Answer: B.

why: Binomial nomenclature (Linnaeus) gives each species a two-part Latin name: the genus followed by the species, e.g. Homo sapiens.

similar.a: E. None of the above. — 'Homo' is the genus – which is not among options A–D. Answer: E.

why: The genus name begins with a capital letter and the species name with a small letter, and both are written in italics (or underlined): Homo sapiens.

C) Some members are photosynthetic autotrophs.  D) Some members of the kingdom are parasites.  E) Majority of the members possess cell wall made up of Chitin.
similar.a: E. Majority of the members possess cell wall made up of Chitin. — Bacterial cell walls are made of peptidoglycan; chitin is the wall material of fungi. Answer: E.
